newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France signs Cuba deal, warns U.S..
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France signs Cuba deal, warns U.S..

text.p: France signed a trade deal with Cuba on Friday and warned the United States not to interfere with French companies doing business in Cuba.
The United States had voiced muted criticism of the agreement on Thursday and added it hoped Paris would continue to fight for human rights on the communist-ruled island.

French Industry Minister Franck Borotra told reporters at the signing ceremony that France and the European Union remained opposed to the extra-territorial application of the Helms-Burton law which seeks to sanction companies doing business with Cuba.
The European Union on Monday asked the World Trade Organisation to suspend a panel looking into the law after the U.S. pledged to soften it.

"We have taken note of the arrangement between the European Commission and the United States," Borotra said. "But this arrangement does not solve the problem. It envisages further contact in order to find a satisfying solution," he said.
"We consider that the panel has only been suspended and should be immediately re-established if the Americans take measures against European companies," Borotra added.
About the U.S. criticism, Borotra said that France was "an independent republic, master of its own decisions."
Ibrahim Ferradaz Garcia, Cuban minister for foreign investments and economic co-operation, said the agreement with France was very important.
"My country is making great efforts to re-integrate, in a competitive framework, the international economy, he said.
Borotra said France would look at the human rights issue, as part of a "critical relationship" with Cuba.
The agreement's main points are that international investors will get a "fair and equitable" treatment as local investors or investors from favoured nations.
It also stipulates strict limitations on expropriations and full and immediate compensation for investors if they occur.
It includes the liberty of transfers and opens the possibility for international arbitrage in case of a conflict between foreign investors and Cuba.
Borotra said France was the 19th country to sign a similar agreement with Cuba since 1993 and the seventh of the 15-member European Union.
He noted only 39 companies were active in Cuba through joint-venture companies and that French investments were "marginal".
"With the pursuit of the economic opening of Cuba, French companies will be able from now to take a more dynamic part in the industrial and commercial development of (Cuba)," he said.
